relatedSnapshot.title: White-label self-serve workspace activation dead-ends on "Workspace plan unavailable" when the partner's Whop workspace plan is not registered
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Source**: Intercom conversation <url:app.intercom.com>

**Bounded conversation context (Sep 8-14)**

Owner of the white-label partner portal Company One LLC (portal host <domain>) is standing up the client workspace "Company Two" (Company Ten) and is blocked at two steps:

* Cold email provider: in the Company Ten workspace, Cold Email Agent > email accounts shows the "Connect a Provider to Buy Email Accounts" modal; clicking Enable Acquisity raises the toast "Unable to switch providers automatically. Please contact support." (screenshot).
* Workspace activation: from the partner portal, <domain>/dashboard/onboarding?step=10 renders "Activate your workspace. / Choose your workspace plan to continue." with the card "Workspace plan unavailable / A workspace plan has not been configured yet. Contact support before continuing." and no action available (screenshot).
* Customer summary: "I paid $185 back on Sept 5th to upgrade the cold email campaign ... I can not connect to email provider and the system is not activated."

**Finding**

Predominant ask is product (get the client workspace working); it is not a money ask.

1. Workspace plan step. For a partner-governed workspace, resolveOnboardingPlanPresentation (apps/web/lib/onboarding/onboarding-plan-presentation.server.ts) resolves the plan via getWhopPlanBySlot(partnerId, WorkspaceMonthly). Partner "Company One LLC" (<uuid>) has no whop partner-scope billing provider config and zero billing_provider_product rows, so the presentation has workspacePlan = null and PlansScreen (apps/web/components/onboarding/onboarding-screens.tsx) takes the empty pricedPlans branch and renders the hard dead-end card above. Partners that do have a whop config (Name 7 AI, Customer Workspace, Name 8 Test) are unaffected. Counted 2026-09-14: 869 partner-governed organizations, of which 169 across 134 partners (all whop-billed) sit under a partner with no configured Whop workspace-monthly plan. The same symptom was filed on 2026-08-05 as ENG-12352 (<domain> // <workspace-slug>), also still in Triage.
2. Provider step. Company Ten has no outreach_provider row and its billing account provider is 'whop', which is the already-tracked partner/whitelabel provider dead-end in ENG-13499. This conversation's earlier report was ENG-13600, already marked Duplicate of ENG-13499.

**Payment, for completeness**

Not the problem. A $185.00 usd partner subscription was paid 2026-09-03 and is active to 2026-10-03, alongside a $10 / 1,000-credit purchase; the app shows the 1,000-credit balance. The customer's Sep 8 observations ("No active subscription found", no Manage Billing button, no managed domains or email accounts) are consistent with the missing plan mapping; worth a second look if the workspace still reads as unsubscribed after the plan is registered.

**Human action needed**

Register the partner's Whop workspace-monthly plan for Company Eight (internal admin only: billing provider config + product sync via partner-billing syncPlan); the partner has no self-serve path to do this, which is why the screen says to contact support. Then confirm whether the Company Ten workspace still needs manual email provider provisioning under ENG-13499.

relatedSnapshot.title: Marketing sidebar has no AI Name 9 in a client workspace under a self-serve white-label partner (Acquisity-controlled ads feature not enabled on the workspace)
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Source**: Intercom conversation <url:app.intercom.com> (follow-up message, 2026-09-14)

**Ask**

"on Company Two Dashboard, under Marketing Tab there is no AI Name 10". This is a second, separate issue from the workspace-activation finding already tracked as ENG-13861.

**Finding**

The Marketing sidebar entry "AI Name 9" (apps/web/lib/sidebar/catalog.ts, key ai-ads-maker, route /dashboard/\[organizationSlug\]/ai-ads-maker) is shown only when the workspace has ADS_CREATOR, ECOM_ADS_MAKER, ECOM_AD_SPY or FACEBOOK_ADS_MANAGER. All of those are Acquisity-controlled partner features (apps/web/lib/features.ts, ACQUISITY_CONTROLLED_PARTNER_FEATURES), and applyAcquisityControlledPartnerFeatureGate (apps/web/lib/auth/feature-access.ts) resolves each of them as: the workspace's own feature flag === true, OR (partner mode is big_client AND the partner config grants it). A self-serve partner cannot grant them, and these keys are excluded from the partner-owner editable set.

Production state for the workspace in question (Company Two, <uuid>): organization.feature_flags is null, and its partner (Company One LLC) is mode self_serve, so every ads feature resolves false and the sidebar entry is hidden. The requester's role there is owner, so the client-role gate (notClient) is not the cause. The partner's own workspace does have ads_creator: true in its feature flags, which is why the tab appears there but not in the client workspace.

Counted 2026-09-14: 133 non-deleted workspaces across 102 self-serve-partner workspaces have no ads feature enabled at workspace level (upper bound for the same gate).

**Human action needed**

An internal admin has to enable the ads feature on that client workspace (admin organization feature flags: ads_creator, or ecom_ads_maker / ecom_ad_spy / facebook_ads_manager as appropriate) if the client is meant to have AI Name 9. Neither the partner nor the workspace can self-serve it.

relatedSnapshot.title: White-label partner clients have no in-app support chat because the partner's chat credentials are unconfigured
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Source

Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>
Contact: the owner of client workspaces under the white-label partner "Company Eleven" (<domain>).

## Bounded conversation context

2026-09-11: the customer opened the portal chat asking for a live agent, then wrote that they have a white label workspace in their white label on their website and need assistance with it, followed by "We did not find a chat room in it. Is there one or can we get help here". A teammate picked the conversation up mid-thread.

## Finding

Not a product defect. The partner's per-partner chat integration is not configured.

* The in-app support chat is the Intercom messenger. For a white-label partner the client app loads the partner's own chat credentials only: the chat component takes the partner's Intercom app id, with no fallback to the platform app id, so when the partner record has no app id the messenger never starts, the lower-right launcher never appears, and the Feedback entry that opens the same messenger does nothing.
* The partner record for "Company Eleven" has no chat app id and no identity-verification secret saved. Its client workspaces are active with onboarding skipped, so this is configuration rather than an outage.
* The entry point itself is not missing: Feedback lives in the bottom-left sidebar profile menu and appears for every member who is not in the client role, so most members should have a working entry once the partner's chat app is configured.
* Blast radius, counted 2026-09-11: 76 active partners (74 self-serve) have no chat app id saved, so their clients have no in-app route to support at all.
* Not a duplicate: no Name 14 issue was found for partner chat credentials going unconfigured.

## Proposed human action

Support/partner ops: confirm the partner's own chat workspace and its identity-verification secret, then save the partner's chat app id (and secret) on the "Company Eleven" partner record so its clients get the launcher and a working Feedback entry. Then reply to this thread telling the customer where support lives in their portal and asking them to paste their issue back into the open conversation.

## Wording note (follow-up, not a defect)

The local support articles tell readers that Feedback in the bottom-left sidebar is the fastest route to support and attribute a missing launcher to ad blockers. That reads badly in a portal where the launcher is absent for a partner-configuration reason. Worth reviewing if partner clients are a supported audience for those articles.

relatedSnapshot.title: Partner/whitelabel workspaces dead-end on "Connect email sending provider" with an unending "In progress" spinner
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Whitelabel/Whop partner workspaces that hold an active subscription but have no email sending provider get permanently stuck on the cold-email onboarding step "Connect email sending provider", which shows an endless "In progress" spinner with no reachable path to recover.

## Problem

A partner workspace with no provider reaches the "Before you create your first campaign" checklist. The provider step renders an animated "In progress" spinner, and both that step's action and the primary "Continue" button are disabled. The workspace has no way to connect a provider or trigger provisioning, so it cannot create campaigns.

## Root cause

In `apps/web/components/campaigns/onboarding/cold-email-onboarding-flow.tsx` the provider step's status is `needsProvider ? (canAdjustProvider ? 'incomplete' : '<stripe-id>') : 'complete'`, so a workspace with `provider_not_configured` and `canAdjustProvider === false` renders a permanent spinner. `checkCanAdjustProvider` (`apps/web/lib/services/outreach-provider.ts`) returns false for a Whop partner org with zero providers on the assumption it will be auto-provisioned, and the only recovery path (provider-selection modal -> `handleEnableAcquisityFlow` -> workspace setup) is gated behind the same `canAdjustProvider` flag, so it is unreachable.

## Blast radius

452 Whop workspaces have an active partner subscription and no `outreach_provider` row (upper bound), counted 2026-09-04. Confirmed affected: 1 workspace.

```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM organization o
JOIN billing_account ba ON ba.id = o.billing_account_id
WHERE ba.provider = 'whop' AND o.deleted_at IS NULL
AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM outreach_provider op WHERE op.organization_id = o.id)
AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM partner_subscription ps
            WHERE ps.organization_id = o.id AND ps.status IN ('active','trialing','past_due'));
```

## Proposed fix

Partner workspaces with an active subscription must either get their provider reliably auto-provisioned, or be given an actionable path (self-serve connection, or an explicit message with a timeline and owner) instead of an unending spinner. The recovery path must not be gated behind the same flag that identifies the stuck state.

## What's included

Fixing the onboarding dead-end and the gating of the recovery path. Excluded until confirmed by a domain expert: whether auto-provisioning on Whop subscription is expected to fire and is silently not firing (needs investigation to pin the exact trigger).

## Regression seam

The provider readiness item in `ColdEmailOnboardingFlow`: a partner workspace with an active subscription and no provider must not remain `<stripe-id>` with a disabled action. Assert that such a workspace is actionable or shows an explicit non-spinner state.

## Done when

* A partner workspace with a subscription and no provider is no longer left on an endless "In progress" spinner.
* The connect/recovery path is reachable for this workspace class.
* A regression test proves the provider step reaches a non-dead-end state for this input.

## Reports

* ENG-13496

relatedSnapshot.title: Self-serve white-label workspaces cannot buy inboxes or domains: checkout fails before payment
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Client workspaces under a self-serve white-label partner can't buy pre-warmed inboxes and domains. Every checkout attempt shows "payment failed", no payment is taken, and the setup step sits on "In progress" until the order expires. After this fix the checkout opens on our Whop store, the client pays, and the inboxes are set up like any other order.

## Problem

Reported on 18 September 2026 by Company Four (<domain>) while onboarding their first client workspace, Company Nine. The client picked 6 domains with 3 Name 20 inboxes each and pressed pay four times between 11:24 and 11:30 UTC. Each attempt failed before reaching Whop, so nothing was charged. The order was then auto-cancelled at 11:40 when the domain reservation expired.

No self-serve partner workspace has ever completed an inbox order. Past Whop inbox orders all came from big-client partners (Customer Workspace, Name 7 AI) that have their own Whop store set up with us. Self-serve partners are meant to use our own Whop store, which already works for their subscriptions, credit top-ups and website domains (ENG-11291). The inbox checkout was never updated to do the same.

## User experience

* Today: Cold Email Agent setup > Setup inboxes > choose domains > pay shows "payment failed". The step stays "In progress" and retrying doesn't help.
* After: the same flow opens a Whop checkout for the order total. After payment, the order moves to provisioning and the inboxes appear as usual.
* If our store isn't configured for this purchase, the customer sees a clear "not available" message, not a generic payment failure.

## Done when

* A self-serve partner's client workspace can check out a pre-warmed inbox order, and the payment starts provisioning.
* Big-client partners' inbox checkout behaves exactly as before.
* After payment, cancelling, repricing and refunding the order use the same store the customer paid in.
* One real low-cost order in a self-serve test workspace completes in production and is refunded afterwards (preview environments cannot complete Whop payments).

## Implementation context

* Failure: `Whop is not configured for this billing provider config` (Sentry ACQUISITY-547). The inbox order checkout only reads partner or platform Whop settings saved in the database. Self-serve partners have none, and no platform Whop row exists.
* Our webhook ignores payments on our own store unless it recognises the product. So the per-order plan must be created under our existing Email product, which the webhook maps to the email slot.
* Follow the self-serve rule from ENG-11291: self-serve partners always use our store, big clients always use their own, with no fallback between them.
* Don't add a platform Whop row in the database as a hotfix. It changes store selection for every partner.

relatedSnapshot.title: Done-for-you domain and email-account orders are refused in self-serve white-label portals ("Checkout unavailable - Self-serve Whop order checkout only supports pre-warmed orders")
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Source**: Intercom conversation <url:app.intercom.com> (follow-up report, 2026-09-24)

**Ask**

The client reports that, after connecting a provider, buying domains and email accounts fails on Purchase with an error saying Whop is not set up for this workspace.

**Finding**

The purchase is being refused by an intentional guard on done-for-you orders in self-serve white-label portals, not by anything missing on the client's or the partner's side.

apps/web/lib/whop/order-plan.ts resolveOrderPlanStore sends a self-serve partner's orders to the platform Whop store (orderPlanStoreForMode maps self_serve to 'platform'), and that branch refuses anything other than pre-warmed orders until DFY trial billing is verified on the platform store. A DFY order therefore returns "Checkout unavailable - Self-serve Whop order checkout only supports pre-warmed orders until trial billing is verified."

Evidence, production, verified 2026-09-24: workspace "Company Ten" (<uuid>, partner Company One LLC) has 7 domain_purchase_order rows created 2026-09-22 and 2026-09-23, every one order_type=dfy, every one status=cancelled, every one carrying exactly that error. No pre-warmed order has been attempted. The same workspace activated correctly (onboarding completed, one outreach_provider row), so the earlier plan-step and provider dead-ends are behind it.

**Why it matters**

The UI still offers done-for-you as a purchase option in these portals, so a paying partner reaches a Purchase button that can only fail, and the message names Whop in a way that reads as a setup problem on their side. No ticket or owner currently covers this restriction; a Name 14 duplicate search for the error string and for DFY purchases in self-serve portals returns nothing.

**Human action needed**

Either verify DFY trial billing on the platform Whop store so these orders can be sold, or stop offering done-for-you in self-serve portals and say so in the UI. Until then the customer-facing answer is to order pre-warmed domains and email accounts, which goes through.
